notes: Reviewed map from Basketball Index (BBI) metric names to the 94 approved player-model inputs. Metric names only; BBI definition text stays in the git-ignored capture catalog. Layers are kept separate: technique inputs (S/F) use rate, per-shot or versus-expected quality metrics; tendency inputs (T) use frequencies, shares and attempt rates; physical inputs (P) use only listed height/weight and weak in-game speed; coach usage, teammates, opponents and on/off impact are context only. direction: +1 means a higher metric value means more of the input (better skill, larger tool, or more frequent choice); -1 the reverse. Direction is about the raw BBI value; check whether a capture stores a percentile already ordered by desirability before applying it. strength: primary = the most direct available measure; supporting = relevant but mixed with other factors; weak = indirect, use only as a small nudge. Every BBI result is an effective on-court observation that also contains physical tools, role and teammates. It constrains the estimate; it is not 'technique only'. Metrics named '... Per 75' must be divided by the relevant exposure (touches, drives, attempts, contests) before informing a skill. A metric listed under several inputs is one shared signal (one correlation group), never independent evidence. BBI 'Talent' grades fold in volume or self-creation, so per-shot 'Shot Making Efficiency' and 'Stable' percentages are preferred as primary. Passing families share three generic recognition metrics and two generic execution metrics; only drive-and-kick, connector, skip and outlet passes have any family-specific signal. For distribution inputs, outcome names the registry outcome the metric informs; T02 outcomes three_corner_share and three_deep_share describe detail within the three region.
